title: Rate Limiting
body:
A server-side cap on how many requests a given client may make in a given window — the kitchen only accepting so many orders per minute. It protects the backend from abuse, runaway retry loops, and expensive scraping, and it's enforced entirely on their machine; nothing the client does can raise the limit.

When exceeded, the server returns **429 Too Many Requests**, usually with a `Retry-After` header telling the client how long to wait. Well-behaved clients honour that and back off exponentially rather than hammering. Limits are typically keyed on API key, user ID, or IP, and third-party APIs (analytics, payment providers) almost always have them — which matters when your frontend fans out a lot of requests at once. See [[HTTP Status Code]].
